youtube.description:
Ads now run in Bing's AI Overviews through campaigns you already have, Performance Max and AI Max included. James and Hannah talk about why the smaller, less watched Microsoft account carries the most risk over Black Friday. They also explain why Bing works as a live test before Google's launch.

Full episode and article: https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/bing-ai-overviews-ads-paid-search/

Microsoft confirmed on 19 November that ads now run in Bing's AI Overviews through existing Performance Max and AI Max campaigns. In a lot of brands the Microsoft budget is the smaller one, and some accounts were imported from Google Ads and left alone.

In this clip from the Manual Focus podcast, Hannah and I explain why I'd treat Bing as a live test for Google's launch. The podcast voices are AI-generated.

The job to hand over is the inventory. Give the AI your campaign export with type, created date, last edited date and spend. It hands back a table of what's eligible, ranked by spend, with the neglected campaigns flagged.

The full episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/bing-ai-overviews-ads-paid-search/
clips.text: Here's where I'd worry as a head of paid. In a lot of brands, the Microsoft budget is the smaller one, so it gets less attention, and some accounts were imported from Google Ads and left alone. Those accounts are now serving into a new placement over Black Friday, and nobody will be able to say whether a change came from the season or from the inventory. And AI Max gets the widest change, because it decides what to match and what the ad says. People ask AI answers in full questions, not the short keywords most accounts were built around. Our view is that you should treat Bing as a live test of the Google launch still to come. Same mechanics, it got there first, and the smaller budget makes mistakes cheaper to find.
